Lec13-Probability

Important: Monte Carlo simulation

13.1.probability and random numbers

Monte Carlo method to estimate pi in R

uniformly sample points, use number of points fall in circle to estimate circle area, thus calculating pi

  • runif(n_iteration, min, max): uniform sampling
  • expand.grid(): creating data.frame, and setNames(c(, )) st the same time
  • or use: data.frame to create data frame directlydf
estimate_pi <- function(n_iter, seed= 42){
  set.seed(seed)
  x<-runif(n_iter,min=-0.5,max=0.5)#sample x axes
  y<-runif(n_iter,min=-0.5,max=0.5)#sample y axes
  dist<-sqrt(x**2+y**2)
  area = mean(dist<=0.5) # within target circle
  pi <- 4*area
  pi
}
n_iters <- c(1e1, 1e2, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5)#不同数量级的取样
seeds <- seq(1:100)
df <- expand.grid(n_iters, seeds) |> setNames(c("n_iter", "seed")) #单列,扩展出两列,形成表格
df$pi_estimates <- mapply(estimate_pi, df$n_iter, df$seed)

visualize the estimation for different n_iter, prepare for LLN

df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=n_iter, y=pi_estimates, group = n_iter)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = pi, linetype = "dashed")+
  geom_boxplot()+ 
  scale_x_log10()

13.2.independence and conditional probability

\(P(A|B) = \frac{P(AB)}{P(B)}\) \(P(AB) = {P(A)}{P(B)}\)

Permutation: getting flush

# Simulations for pokers
suits <- c("Diamonds", "Clubs", "Hearts", "Spades")
numbers <- c(
  "Ace", "Deuce", "Three", "Four", "Five", "Six", "Seven", 
  "Eight", "Nine", "Ten", "Jack", "Queen", "King")
deck <- expand.grid(number=numbers, suit=suits)
deck <- paste(deck$number, deck$suit)
sample(deck, 5, replace=FALSE)
[1] "Five Clubs"   "Queen Spades" "Seven Clubs"  "Nine Hearts"  "King Clubs"

\(P(A) = P(B|A) = P(C|A) = 0.25 \Rightarrow ABC, independent\)

# Three-card scenarios
three_card_combinations <- permutations(52, 3, v=deck)

heart_cards <- paste(numbers, "Hearts")
p_first_is_heart <- mean(three_card_combinations[,1] %in% heart_cards)
p_second_is_heart <- mean(three_card_combinations[,2] %in% heart_cards)
p_third_is_heart <- mean(three_card_combinations[,3] %in% heart_cards)

p_all_are_heart <- mean(
  three_card_combinations[,1] %in% heart_cards &
  three_card_combinations[,2] %in% heart_cards &
  three_card_combinations[,3] %in% heart_cards)

print(p_first_is_heart * p_second_is_heart * p_third_is_heart)
[1] 0.015625
print(p_all_are_heart)
[1] 0.01294118
# Event A: first card is heart
# Event B: second card is heart
# Event C: third card is heart
# P(A)
three_card_combinations |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  summarize(first_is_heart = mean(V1 %in% heart_cards))

# P(B|A)
three_card_combinations |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(V1 %in% heart_cards) |>
  summarize(second_is_heart = mean(V2 %in% heart_cards))

# P(C|A,B)
three_card_combinations |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  filter(V1 %in% heart_cards & V2 %in% heart_cards) |>
  summarize(second_is_heart = mean(V3 %in% heart_cards))
is_flush <- function(seed = NA){
  if(!is.na(seed)){
    set.seed(seed) #for setting random seed
  }
  hand <- sample(deck, 5, replace=FALSE) ## without replacement
  suit_in_hand <- str_split(hand, "\\s", simplify = TRUE) 
  # simplify: 回归矩阵形式, "<number> <suit(type)>"
  length(unique(suit_in_hand[,2]))==1 #same suit => flush
}
set.seed(32)
mean(replicate(1e5, is_flush()))
[1] 0.00207

Combination: getting a natural 21

# Natural 21 : getting aces and facecard in the first draw
aces <- paste("Ace", suits)
facecard <- paste(c("King", "Queen", "Jack", "Ten"), suits)

# MC simulation of getting natural 21
is_21 <- function(seed=NA){
  if (!is.na(seed)){
    set.seed(seed)
  }
  hand <- sample(deck, 2, replace=FALSE)
  flag1 <- hand[[1]] %in% aces & hand[[2]] %in% facecard
  flag2 <- hand[[2]] %in% aces & hand[[1]] %in% facecard
  flag1 | flag2
}
set.seed(42)
mean(replicate(1e5, is_21())) # probablity to get natural 21

13.4.LLN, CLT

\[ E(X)\approx \overline{X};\; SD(X)\approx \frac{1}{n}\Sigma({X_i}P(X_i))^2;\; \]

\[ E(\overline{X})=E(X_i);\; SD(\overline{X})=\frac{SD(X_i)}{\sqrt{n}};\; \]

13.5.Case study: Bank loan

default_rate: fail to pay back

interest_rate: target variable, too small not enough to make up bad debt, too large will result in losing existing customers

# Case study: loan
principal_per_loan <- 180000
operational_loss <- 20000
loss_per_foreclosure <- -(principal_per_loan + operational_loss)

main simulator function

sim_average_return <- function(interest_rate=0.02, default_rate=0.02, loans=1000){
  defaults <- sample( #seq indicating default or not
      c(0,1), loans, prob=c(1-default_rate, default_rate), replace = TRUE)
  balance <- #return = revenue - cost(loss)
    sum(defaults * loss_per_foreclosure) +
      sum((1 - defaults) * principal_per_loan * interest_rate)
  balance / loans 
  #average revenue(balance)
}

Case1: fixed 2% interest rate

Lec14-Statistical inference

14.1.Basics

\(sample\,characteristic\Rightarrow\,intrinsic\,population\,charicteristic\)

  • spread: p1-p2

  • MoE(margin of error)

#poll from a jar of beads
p<-0.4
population_size<-1e7
jar<-sample(c(1,0),population_size,prob=c(p,1-p),replace=TRUE)#creating the population
#estimate p by sampling
take_sample<-function(n){
  sample<-sample(c(1,0),n,prob=c(p,1-p),replace=TRUE)
  mean(sample)
}

result<-data.frame(
  estimate_prop=replicate(1e4,take_sample(25))
)
result|>ggplot(aes(estimate_prop))+
  geom_histogram(binwidth=0.04)

result<-data.frame(
  estimate_prop=replicate(1e4,take_sample(1000))
)
result|>ggplot(aes(estimate_prop))+
  geom_histogram(binwidth=0.001)

#choosing binwidth: n*binwidth>1

14.2.SD,SE,CI

\[ sample\,mean: E(\overline{X})=E(X_i)=p; \]

\[ sample\,variance: Var(\overline{X}=\frac{Var(X_i)}{n}=\frac{p(1-p)}{n} \]

\[ standard\,error\,: SE(\overline{X})=SD(\overline{X})=\sqrt{\frac{p(1-p)}{n}} \]

\[ Margin\,of\,error: MoE(X)=2*SE(X) \]

  • CTL: when sample_size increases, our estimation is more “accurate”, we are more “confident”
    given that: SE decreases
sample_sizes<-seq(1,1e4,2)
result<-data.frame(
  sample_size=sample_sizes,
  SE=sqrt(p*(1-p)/sample_sizes)
)
Error: object 'p' not found

\[ CLT \Rightarrow \overline{X}\sim N(\mu,\sigma) \]

\[ 95\%\,confidence: [\overline{X}\pm 1.96*SE(X)] \]

# Confidence interval
take_sample_and_check <- function(n){
  sampled_beads<-sample(jar,n,replace=TRUE)
  X_bar<-mean(sampled_beads)
  X_SE<-sqrt(X_bar*(1-X_bar)/n) # 95
  #assume we don't know p, so use X_bar sample parameter to estimate during calculation
  between(p,X_bar-1.96*X_SE,X_bar+1.96*X_SE)
  #<bool> check if p is within CI
}
set.seed(42)
mean(replicate(1e4, take_sample_and_check(1000)))
mean(replicate(1e4, take_sample_and_check(25)))

# Power analysis at different p
ps <- c(0.501, 0.51, 0.53, 0.55, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8)
sample_size <- c(10, 30, 100, 300, 1000, 3000, 1e4, 3e4, 1e5, 3e5, 1e6, 3e6)
power_analysis <- expand.grid(p=ps, n=sample_size)
power_analysis <- power_analysis |>
  mutate(se=sqrt(p * (1-p) / n)) |>
  mutate(CI_lower=p - se * 1.95, CI_upper=p + se * 1.96)
power_analysis |>
  mutate(p = factor(p)) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_line(aes(x=n, y=CI_lower, color=p)) +
  geom_line(aes(x=n, y=CI_upper, color=p), lty="dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept=0.5, color="black") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0.49, 0.51)) +
  ylab("CI on estimate of p") +
  xlab("Sample size") +
  theme_minimal()

Lec15-Bayes theorem

15.1.Basics

\[ P(A|B)=\frac{P(B|A)P(A)}{P(B)}\\ B: observation; A:target\\ P(B):evidence证据概率\\ P(A):prior先验概率,initial,belief\\ P(B|A):likelihood似然度,证据B对A的支持程度\\ P(A|B):posterior后验概率, new,belief \]

15.2.Case study: lung cancer and pulmonary nodules

$ B: pulmonary,nodule; A:Lung,cancer\ Aim: P(A|B) $

potential bias: \(P(A),P(B)\) not from same population \(\Leftarrow\) condition on the same population when sampling

15.3.Bayesian VS frequentist

  • Bayesian modeling of coin toss: observed two heads
    no pre-assumption on p (different from frequentist)

    \[ P(p|2H)=\frac{P(2H|p)P(p)}{P(2H)},\,for\,p\in [0,1]\ \]

# Bayesian modeling of coin toss: observed two heads
df <- data.frame(p=seq(0, 1, 0.01))
df <- df |> mutate(posterior=p**2)

step_size <- 0.01  # Approximate the area under the curve
total_area <- sum(df$posterior * step_size)
df <- df |> mutate(posterior = posterior / total_area)  # Normalize

df |> ggplot(aes(p, posterior)) +
  geom_line() +
  ylab("Probability density (posterior)") +
  theme_minimal()
  • 10H/14 tosses, estimate 2H in the next 2 toss
    no pre-assumption about p,
    assume uniform, if prior distribution is not given
```r
# Bayesian modeling of coin toss: observed 10 heads out of 14 tosses
cons = length(combinations(14, 10))
#the combinartorial number C(14,10)
df <- data.frame(p=seq(0, 1, 0.01))#all possible value of p
df <- df |> mutate(posterior=cons * ((1 - p)**4) * (p**10))

step_size <- 0.01
total_area <- sum(df$posterior * step_size)
df <- df |> mutate(posterior = posterior / total_area)  
#Normalize

df |> ggplot(aes(p, posterior)) +
  geom_line() +
  ylab("Probability density (posterior)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

16.2.Regression

using one variable to indicate another one

\[begin{align} correlation\,coefficient:\rho=\frac{1}{n}\Sigma^{n}_{i=1}(\frac{x_i-\mu_x}{\sigma_x})(\frac{y_i-\mu_y}{\sigma_y})\\ regression\,line: y=b+mx\\ slope\,coefficient:m=\rho\frac{\sigma_x}{\sigma_y}=\frac{\Sigma(X_i-\overline{X})(Y_i-\overline{Y})}{\Sigma(X_i-\overline{X})^2}\\ intersection:b=\mu_y-\mu_x\\ \]

  group_by(family) |>
  sample_n(1) |>  # Sample one child per family
  ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(father, childHeight) |>
  rename(son = childHeight)

```r

model <- lm(son ~ father, data=galton_heights)
galton_heights |>
  ggplot(aes(father, son)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.5) +
  geom_abline(
    slope=model$coefficients[2],
    intercept=model$coefficients[1]) +
  theme_minimal()
```
